provenance: What each class contributes to a split, as parts. Transcribed from each class file's `## Dip value` section plus its subclass table. WORKED EXAMPLE ONLY — Rogue and Fighter are populated so the shape can be checked; the other fifteen classes are not yet written. Composition feeds the split *filter*, never a published number: see SKILL.md.

schema.id: `<class>/<levels>` for the class-generic part, `<class>/<levels>/<subclass>` for a subclass-specific one. A build takes the generic part AND at most one subclass part at the same level.
schema.as_first: Applies only when this class is the character's LEVEL 1 class. Exactly one class in a split is first. Saving throws and the good armour come from here and nowhere else.
schema.as_dip: Applies when the class is entered after level 1. Same levels, much less: no saving throws, reduced armour, one skill instead of four.
schema.grants: SET-VALUED, never summed. `prof` unions into the save set and is then scored by derive_saves(); `armour` takes the best category across all parts; `shield` is a boolean OR; `skills` and `expertise` sum but feed the skl rubric rather than an axis directly.
schema.deltas: The genuinely additive part, in axis rungs. Summed across parts, then clamped to 0-5. These are FILTER-GRADE estimates.
schema.requires: Condition on the rest of the build, or null. `{"primary": "cha"}` means the part is worth its deltas only on a Charisma body; otherwise deltas are halved.
schema.conflicts: Tags this part competes for. Two parts sharing a tag do not stack — the larger delta applies and the smaller is dropped. `bonus-action-attack` is capped by Lone Wolf's two Bonus Actions; `extra-attack` never stacks.
schema.exit: What the class gives up by stopping at N levels instead of 20. Keyed by the level stopped at. Applied to the PRIMARY class only, since a dip never had those levels to lose.

conflict_tags.extra-attack: Extra Attack does not stack from two sources.
conflict_tags.bonus-action-attack: Lone Wolf grants two Bonus Actions; a third source has nowhere to go.
conflict_tags.expertise: Expertise on the same skill twice is wasted; the skl rubric saturates.
conflict_tags.sneak-attack: One Sneak Attack per turn regardless of source.

rogue/1.note: The Expertise argument is about Rogue 1, not the dip. Multiclassing *into* Rogue grants light armour and one skill, no Expertise.

rogue/2.note: Cunning Action: Dash / Disengage / Hide as a Bonus Action.

rogue/3.note: The standard Rogue dip: Cunning Action plus a subclass. Sneak Attack 2d6.

rogue/3/Thief.note: A second Bonus Action, on top of Lone Wolf's extra one. The strongest three-level dip in the list.

rogue/3/Assassin.note: Action and Bonus Action restored at the start of combat; guaranteed crits on the surprised.

rogue/3/Swashbuckler.note: Sneak Attack with no advantage and no adjacent ally required.

rogue/3/Inquisitive.note: Insightful Fighting as a repeatable Sneak Attack enabler.

rogue/5.note: Extends the dip to Uncanny Dodge and Cunning Strike.

rogue/9.note: Sneak Attack 5d6, Evasion at 7, second Expertise pair at 6, subclass feature at 9. At-will damage, so endurance rises.

fighter/1.note: Heavy armour and shields even as a dip; Second Wind. Str+Con saves only when first.

fighter/2.note: Action Surge. The single best two levels for action economy in the list.

fighter/11.note: Improved Extra Attack — three attacks per Action, six per round under Lone Wolf — plus the off-cadence feat at 11.

fighter/11/Battle Master.note: Superiority dice on the short-rest clock; manoeuvres carry riders and control.

cleric/1.note: Wis+Cha saves only when first; light/medium/shields, Wis casting and the domain's whole level-1 kit from any position, but Goon's fix means a Cleric multiclass grants NO skills.

cleric/2.note: Channel Divinity (1 charge, short rest) plus Turn Undead — the level to stop at when the domain's Channel Divinity is the reason for the dip.

cleric/3.note: Feat-neutral under Listo's cadence, but buys only level-2 slots and the level-3 domain spell pair.

cleric/5.note: Destroy Undead and level-3 spells — the first level the Cleric's own spell list carries area control rather than riding the domain.

cleric/6.note: Second Channel Divinity charge on the short-rest clock plus the domain's tier-2 feature; the last level that reads as a dip rather than a commitment.

cleric/1/Tempest.note: Heavy armour, martial weapons and Wrath of the Storm — the classic one-level dip for a Dex-light caster (the dur rung stands in for the domain's heavy-armour grant, which the class-generic part cannot carry).

cleric/1/Life.note: Heavy armour plus Disciple of Life, which boosts every healing spell the character casts from any source.

cleric/1/War.note: Heavy armour, martial weapons and War Priest's bonus-action attack, 3 per long rest.

cleric/1/Zeal.note: Strictly a wider offer than War 1 for a dip: same heavy armour and martial weapons, but the bonus-action attack has Wis-modifier uses and needs no level-6 Extra Attack to pay off.

cleric/1/Order.note: Heavy armour, and Voice of Authority turns every buff or heal on your partner into a free weapon attack from them.

cleric/1/Peace.note: No armour upgrade, but Emboldening Bond is a permanent d4 on both characters' attacks, checks and saves in a two-body party.

cleric/1/Forge.note: Heavy armour and a long-rest +1 AC or +1 weapon blessing; the real payoff (+1 AC in heavy, then physical resistance) is six and seventeen levels deep.

cleric/1/Inquisition.note: Heavy armour, martial weapons and Witch Hunter's Strike — +1d8 force, doubled with temp HP against a concentrating caster.

cleric/1/Twilight.note: Heavy armour, martial weapons, 90m darkvision and a +3 initiative touch; the domain's real offer sits at level 2.

cleric/1/Grave.note: Circle of Mortality maximises healing on a downed character and gives free bonus-action Spare the Dying — a cheap answer to the duo's drop-and-lose failure mode.

cleric/1/Arcana.note: Two wizard cantrips that count as Cleric cantrips plus Arcana proficiency; Counterspell only arrives with the level-5 domain spells.

cleric/1/Nature.note: The only domain with built-in Shillelagh access, so a Wisdom melee build pays no feat tax — heavy armour and a nature skill on top.

cleric/1/Death.note: Martial weapons and Reaper, which makes a single-target cantrip hit two creatures; no heavy armour.

cleric/1/Strength.note: Heavy armour, a druid cantrip and a physical skill, but no martial weapons; Haste on the domain list needs Cleric 5.

cleric/1/Knowledge.note: Double proficiency bonus in two of Arcana/History/Nature/Religion — Expertise in all but name, and the only thing the domain sells at one level.

cleric/1/Light.note: Warding Flare imposes disadvantage on an attack for a reaction, and Lone Wolf's spare reaction means it costs nothing already spoken for.

cleric/2/Twilight.note: Twilight Sanctuary is a per-round temp-HP tap on both characters plus a charm/fright cleanse, for one short-rest Channel Divinity charge.

cleric/2/Inquisition.note: Spell Shield hands a creature temp HP with spell resistance and advantage on spell saves while they hold — in a duo that covers half the party.

cleric/2/Grave.note: Path to the Grave gives the target vulnerability to all damage on the next hit, timed onto your partner's biggest swing.

cleric/2/Tempest.note: Destructive Wrath maximises thunder and lightning damage, and Goon moved the trigger to when damage lands so the charge is never wasted.

cleric/2/Zeal.note: Consuming Fervor maximises fire or thunder — with Fireball on the domain list from level 5 this is the biggest single Channel Divinity payout.

cleric/2/Peace.note: Balm of Peace heals 2d6 + Wis to everything you walk past without provoking.

cleric/2/Eldritch.note: Prophecy of Doom is the widest crowd control in the domain list from one charge, but the effect rolled is random.

cleric/2/Strength.note: Feat of Strength adds +10 to a Strength roll and Avatar of Battle I is a 3-turn +1d4 damage transform.

cleric/6/War.note: CCC gives War Domain true Extra Attack at 6, and War Priest stacks on top of it.

cleric/6/Grave.note: Sentinel at Death's Door turns a critical hit on either character into a normal hit, Wis-modifier times per long rest, for a reaction Lone Wolf leaves spare.

cleric/6/Forge.note: Soul of the Forge adds fire resistance and +1 AC in heavy armour, which is the level Forge starts paying for itself.

cleric/6/Order.note: Embodiment of the Law casts an enchantment spell as a bonus action, Wis-modifier times per long rest.

ranger/1.note: The cheapest Str+Dex save pair in the game and only as the level-1 class; martial weapons, medium armour, shields, Favored Foe and a Favoured Enemy pick (which can instead be heavy armour via Ranger Knight or a short-rest Find Familiar) survive a late dip, but the skill grant drops from 3 to 1.

ranger/2.note: Archery (+2 to ranged attacks) or another Fighting Style, plus half-caster entry with two always-prepared spells — the cheapest fighting style outside Fighter.

ranger/3.note: Feat-neutral under Listo's cadence: a full conclave and the level-3 feat for three levels.

ranger/5.note: Extra Attack and Summon Beast; rarely correct unless the other class has no Extra Attack of its own.

ranger/3/Beast Master.note: Expansion moves Companion's Bond to level 3, so three levels buy a PB-scaled third body that saves like a PC and can Help — revive or grant advantage — as a bonus action.

ranger/3/Gloom Stalker.note: Dread Ambusher's +3 initiative and first-round extra attack with +1d8, plus short-rest Umbral Shroud invisibility.

ranger/3/Monster Slayer.note: Slayer's Prey is a +1d6 rider that uses no concentration, so it stacks with Hunter's Mark, and it re-designates on a short rest.

ranger/3/Hunter.note: Hunter's Prey — Colossus Slayer's +1d8, Giant Killer's reaction attack or Horde Breaker's second target; the AoE (Volley) is eight levels later.

ranger/3/Swarmkeeper.note: Gathered Swarm is a once-per-round 1d6, a status (Moths' Blind is a full attack shutdown) or a free reposition, and it wants Hunter's Mark up permanently.

ranger/3/Drakewarden.note: A drake third body whose Infused Strikes adds 1d6 to your partner's weapon attacks as well as your own; the author warns it may need a fresh playthrough.

ranger/3/Fey Wanderer.note: Otherworldly Glamour adds your Wisdom modifier to every Charisma check, making the Ranger the party face without Charisma investment, plus a +1d4 psychic rider.

ranger/3/Horizon Walker.note: Planar Warrior converts all of an attack's damage to Force and adds +1d8, which deletes Listo's resistance-heavy enemy design as a problem.

ranger/3/Primeval Guardian.note: Guardian Soul is temp HP every turn and +5 ft reach for a crippling drop to 5 ft of movement — a bow build, never a charging one.

ranger/3/Snowlight Conclave.note: Glaring Frost blinds on any Cold or Radiant damage you deal, plus Cold resistance — the hardest control conclave, but it needs a Cold or Radiant damage source in gear to function at all.

ranger/3/Conclave of the Dawnstriders.note: Valkyrie is a leaping Action attack that grants an Extra Attack on landing and disadvantage on attacks against you, with Radiant or Fire conversion on every weapon hit.

paragon/1.note: As the opener it returns two feats (Moderately and Heavily Armoured), three from zero armour proficiency, on top of Con+Cha saves; a late dip loses the heavy armour, the saves and the skills but keeps shields, martial weapons and two short-rest Willpower Dice.

paragon/2.note: Fighting Style from the widened UA menu plus Actions Speak Louder, which puts Help and Distract on a Bonus Action.

paragon/3.note: Feat-neutral and works from any position: a full Heroic Title, Fighting Style, Actions Speak Louder and 2 Willpower Dice.

paragon/5.note: Extra Attack, the Willpower Die up to d6, and the Taunting and Feinting Blades; only matters on a chassis without Extra Attack.

paragon/3/Lionheart.note: Banner Lord's Cha-modifier charges buy an ally reaction attack, a free ally dash or +Cha AC — but they stay on the long-rest clock until Paragon 6, which makes the full package a commitment rather than a dip.

paragon/3/Nighthawk.note: Searing Blade strips all resistances for 3 turns on a failed Con save, which makes your partner's damage type stop mattering.

paragon/3/Prodigy.note: Innate Mastery's +1 attack and damage plus Sheer Will's temp HP and flat damage reduction, which compounds with Lone Wolf's already-halved incoming numbers.

paragon/3/Regent.note: Shifting Court swaps your position with the target's on a Help or Distract, pulling the fragile partner out of a pack, and Oberon's Favor adds a Willpower Die of Psychic per attack.

paragon/3/Spellblade.note: Scholar's Armament makes a main-hand weapon use Charisma for attack and damage — a Hexblade-shaped dip no other class in the list provides — plus two elemental Focuses and Arcana expertise; Will Over Weave is ten levels past this.

paragon/3/Sword Saint.note: Falling Rain is a free-action weapon attack riding on every Willpower Die you spend, so more Actions convert directly into more attacks.

bloodhunter/1.note: Martial weapons, medium armour, shields and two short-rest Blood Curses that mostly have no saving throw, so a low-Intelligence body still gets nearly full value; Int+Dex saves only when first.

bloodhunter/2.note: A Fighting Style and Crimson Rite — a permanent-until-long-rest elemental rider on a weapon for a one-time self-hit, which is close to free damage for any martial.

bloodhunter/3.note: Feat-neutral: an Order plus a third Blood Maledict charge.

bloodhunter/5.note: Extra Attack and the hemocraft die up to 1d6; redundant if the base class already has Extra Attack.

bloodhunter/3/Order of the Ghostslayer.note: The highest-value 3-level dip in the class: a fourth Radiant Rite, Necrotic resistance, a fourth Blood Maledict and curses that ignore the Bloodless restriction.

bloodhunter/3/Order of the Lycan.note: Hybrid Transformation 3/short rest gives non-magical physical resistance, +1 AC, Dex-scaling unarmed strikes and a bonus-action strike — at the cost of a Bloodlust save that can turn you on your partner below half HP.

bloodhunter/3/Order of the Mutant.note: A short-rest Mutagen charge and four formulae; Potency and Celerity are +3 to a raw ability score with Listo's cap removed, but every resistance mutagen hands out a matching vulnerability.

bloodhunter/3/Order of the Profane Soul.note: Pact Magic off Intelligence on short-rest slots — one level-1 slot at Blood Hunter 3, so it needs real Intelligence investment and never becomes a primary caster.

inquisitor/1.note: The best Wisdom-save opener that also brings martial weapons, medium armour, shields, a +1/+1 deity weapon and 2 short-rest Judgment charges; the multiclass node itself is undocumented, so the as_dip grants are the file's best guess and only the saves are certainly level-1-locked.

inquisitor/2.note: The sweet spot on a Wisdom body: Righteous Vigilance stacks Wis onto initiative on top of Dex, plus half-caster entry and Monster Lore.

inquisitor/3.note: Feat-neutral: permanent Detect Thoughts via Interrogative Mind plus a full subclass feature.

inquisitor/5.note: Extra Attack, Sanctified Slayer and a third Judgment charge — past this the file says take it as a main class or not at all.

inquisitor/3/Tactics Inquisition.note: Shared Judgment gives your one partner every active Judgment on a short-rest clock, and Tempered Champion upgrades the copy they get.

inquisitor/3/Vengeance Inquisition.note: Monster Tactician is Expertise plus double Wisdom modifier on one Intelligence skill, and Divine Scourge turns every Judgment into a personal upgrade against your Quarry.

inquisitor/3/Zeal Inquisition.note: In-combat fast healing, a delayed damage pool that also buys saves, and Wrathful Taunt giving Judged enemies disadvantage attacking anyone but you — long-rest-free sustain in a 120-supply economy.

sorcerer/1.note: The multiclass node grants nothing at all — no saves, no armour, no skills, no weapons — so Sorcerer 1 as a dip buys only the bloodline's level-1 feature.

sorcerer/1/Draconic Bloodline.note: Unarmoured AC 13 and +1 HP per Sorcerer level — the only thing in the class that patches the d6 and the no-armour problem.

sorcerer/1/Shadow Magic.note: Strength of the Grave: on reaching 0 HP regain 1 instead of going down, which on a duo is a fight that does not end.

sorcerer/1/Favored Soul.note: Medium armour, shields and a Cleric domain's spells as Charisma Sorcerer spells at level 1 — healing and Revivify that Metamagic can Twin.

sorcerer/1/Aberrant Mind.note: Psionic Spells off-list and free of the known-spells budget, plus a Frighten rider on crits.

sorcerer/2.note: Font of Magic: slots to sorcery points and back, both bonus actions — a spell-slot battery bolted onto another caster.

sorcerer/3.note: Three Metamagic picks: Twinned turns every single-target buff into a party-wide one on a two-person party, and Quickened is the only reliable third cast in a turn.

sorcerer/5.note: Third-level slots: Fireball, Haste, and Twinned Haste covering the whole duo for one point per slot level.

sorcerer/6.note: Same generic package as 5 plus six sorcery points; the tier-2 bloodline feature is what level 6 actually sells.

sorcerer/6/Draconic Bloodline.note: Elemental Affinity adds Charisma modifier to every hit of your ancestry's damage type — with the expanded ancestries that now includes Force, Radiant, Necrotic and Psychic.

sorcerer/6/Aberrant Mind.note: Psychic resistance plus Advantage against Charmed and Frightened, and Psionic Sorcery casts the whole psionic list off points with no verbal or somatic components.

sorcerer/6/Favored Soul.note: Extra Attack on a full-caster chassis that already has medium armour and shields.

sorcerer/6/Wild Magic.note: Bend Luck spends a reaction and 2 points to swing any visible creature's attack, check or save by 1d4 either way — and Lone Wolf grants a spare reaction to spend on it.

sorcerer/6/Storm Sorcery.note: Heart of the Storm chips every nearby enemy on Lightning/Thunder casts and adds resistance to both, on top of level 1's bonus-action flight.

sorcerer/11.note: Sixth-level slots, a fourth Metamagic at 10, eleven sorcery points, and the tier-3 bloodline feature — the deepest split a Sorcerer is worth holding as the minority class.

bard/1.note: Three skills from an eighteen-skill list and Dex + Cha saves only when first; a later dip gets light armour, one skill and an instrument.

bard/2.note: Jack of All Trades covers every skill you did not pick, and Song of Rest is a party-wide short rest in a run where long rests cost 120+ supplies.

bard/3.note: The headline dip: a College, Expertise x2, and a feat-neutral cost under Listo's every-three-levels cadence.

bard/3/College of Lore.note: Three extra skill proficiencies on top of Bard's own three, plus Cutting Words as a reaction debuff on any enemy attack, check or damage roll.

bard/3/College of Swords.note: Medium armour, scimitars, a Fighting Style from Listo's widened list, and Blade Flourishes with Goon's interrupt versions that spend a spare reaction.

bard/3/College of Valour.note: The only College handing out shields plus martial weapons — the cheapest way to make a Charisma caster durable without a martial dip.

bard/3/College of Eloquence.note: Unsettling Words is a cheap pre-rolled save debuff you can see the number on before committing the control spell.

bard/3/College of Dance.note: Dexterity unarmed attacks scaling off the Inspiration die, plus a free kick every time you inspire your partner; note it never gets Extra Attack.

bard/3/College of Tragedy.note: Poetry in Misery can refund an Inspiration every turn off natural 1s, and Sorrowful Fate rewrites a save into a Charisma save.

bard/3/College of Stormcalling.note: The only blaster College: a Thunder cantrip and Concussion, which strips enemy reactions and caps them to one action.

bard/5.note: Font of Inspiration moves Bardic Inspiration to the short-rest clock and the die to d8, and third-level slots bring Hypnotic Pattern and Haste — the real Bard breakpoint, not 3.

bard/6.note: Countercharm gives both characters Advantage on Charmed and Frightened saves, and the second College feature lands here.

bard/6/College of Lore.note: Magical Secrets four levels early — two spells from any list the modlist installs, on a six-level chassis.

bard/6/College of Swords.note: Extra Attack on the martial Bard, stacking with Lone Wolf's extra Action.

bard/6/College of Valour.note: Extra Attack on top of shields and martial weapons.

bard/6/College of Eloquence.note: Unfailing Inspiration refunds the die whenever the roll it was spent on fails, which on a duo is almost always your partner's roll.

bard/6/College of Stormcalling.note: Conductor plus bonus-action Staccato Lightning gives a Charisma-scaled second cast every turn while concentrating.

bard/10.note: Magical Secrets x2, which `Automatic Magical Secrets Extender` widens to every list the modlist installs — the single largest grant in the build space — plus a d10 die, a second Expertise pair and fifth-level slots.

artificer/1.note: Medium armour and shields from either position — worth two feats to a caster — while Int + Con saves, two skills and the weapon proficiencies only come from the level-1 node.

artificer/2.note: Two Infusion Slots and four known infusions: Enhanced Weapon, Enhanced Defense, Enhanced Arcane Focus and the Homunculus, all permanent stat for a gear-poor pair.

artificer/3.note: The weak stop: feat-neutral and it buys a subclass, but the base feature is a thieves'-tools conjure and every subclass is back-loaded.

artificer/3/Alchemist.note: Experimental Elixirs twice per long rest, extendable by burning spell slots.

artificer/3/Armorer.note: Arcane Armor grants Heavy Armour proficiency plus built-in Thunder Gauntlets or a Lightning Launcher that work with empty hands.

artificer/3/Artillerist.note: The Eldritch Cannon is a resummonable extra body with Flamethrower, Force Ballista and Protector modes.

artificer/3/Battle Smith.note: Battle Ready puts Intelligence on attack and damage with any magical weapon — which the class's own Enhanced Weapon supplies — plus martial weapons and the Steel Defender.

artificer/5.note: Second-level slots, and the level where Armorer and Battle Smith collect Extra Attack.

artificer/5/Armorer.note: Extra Attack on the heavy-armoured artificer.

artificer/5/Battle Smith.note: Extra Attack with Intelligence driving attack, damage, spell DC and saves off one stat.

artificer/5/Artillerist.note: Arcane Firearm adds 1d8 to a damage roll on every spell you cast, a flat floor that needs no resource.

artificer/5/Alchemist.note: Alchemical Savant adds Intelligence to a roll of any healing or acid/fire/necrotic/poison spell.

artificer/6.note: A third Infusion Slot, six infusions known, and Expertise in the free Sleight of Hand proficiency.

artificer/11.note: Flash of Genius at 7 adds Intelligence to your partner's checks and saves off a reaction, and Spell-Storing Item at 11 hands the other character Int-mod castings of a spell they could never cast.

barbarian/1.note: Str + Con saves, the d12 and armour proficiency only when first; a late dip grants weapons and shields only, but Rage's +2 damage and physical resistance land from any position.

barbarian/2.note: Reckless Attack as a toggle that Goon's extends to thrown attacks — near-permanent Advantage for a Str attacker — plus Danger Sense's Advantage on Dex saves.

barbarian/3.note: Feat-neutral: a subclass plus a third Rage charge, but only the front-loaded paths pay off here.

barbarian/3/Path of the Zealot.note: Divine Fury is +1d6 + half Barbarian level on the first hit each turn, and Warrior of the Gods lets the partner revive you without a scroll.

barbarian/3/Path of the Revenant.note: Heavy armour proficiency and flat damage reduction 2 on top of physical resistance at level 3, at the cost of being unhealable while raging — the `no-healing` tag marks that clash with a healer partner.

barbarian/3/Path of Ginnungagap.note: Advantage on saves against spells patches the class's Wis/Cha hole, plus one reaction crit-downgrade per Rage.

barbarian/5.note: Extra Attack and Fast Movement; the file argues past 3 the class wants to be the main, so this is a majority split rather than a dip.

paladin/1.note: Heavy armour and the Wis + Cha saves come only from the level 1 class; a late dip gets light/medium and shields, plus Channel Oath on the short rest and Lay on Hands either way.

paladin/2.note: Divine Smite converts any spell slot from any class into burst weapon damage, plus half-caster slots of its own.

paladin/3.note: Oath features, oath spells and a second Channel Oath option — feat-neutral, so better shaped than Paladin 2.

paladin/3/Oath of Devotion.note: Sacred Weapon and Holy Rebuke; the safe pick whose real payoff is the charm-immunity aura at 7.

paladin/3/Oath of Vengeance.note: Vow of Enmity is single-target Advantage on a short-rest charge, worth more with Lone Wolf's extra Action to spend it on.

paladin/3/Oath of the Crown.note: A taunt-and-tank Channel Oath that pulls attacks onto the armoured half of the duo.

paladin/3/Oathbreaker.note: Spiteful Suffering and Dreadful Aspect, but Listo replaces Divine Smite outright with Unholy Smite — all-necrotic damage, a straight downgrade through Act 2.

paladin/3/Oath of Conquest.note: Conquering Presence is an AoE Wisdom-save fear and Guided Strike is +10 to an attack roll chosen after seeing it.

paladin/3/Oath of the Bleak Walkers.note: Black Flames as a Bonus Action rider that stacks with Divine Smite, Death's Maw's proficiency-bonus damage reduction near a corpse, and Expertise in Intimidation from level 1.

paladin/3/Oath of the Moon.note: Divine Guardian halves all damage on the other character for 10 turns off a short-rest Channel Oath charge.

paladin/5.note: Extra Attack, which doubles the number of hits a stored spell slot can be smited into.

paladin/6.note: Aura of Protection adds the Charisma modifier to both characters' saving throws at Listo's 9m radius — registered as a booster, not a rung.

paladin/7.note: The oath aura stacks a second party-wide effect on Aura of Protection; the file calls 7 the natural stopping point before committing further.

paladin/7/Oath of the Ancients.note: Aura of Warding gives both characters resistance to spell damage at 9m — the damage type Listo's revamped enemy casters lean on hardest.

paladin/7/Oath of the Moon.note: Aura of Moonlight cuts every hit on either character by the Charisma modifier and stacks with resistance.

paladin/7/Oath of the Bleak Walkers.note: A stacking crit-range reduction that applies to both characters, compounding with Lone Wolf's extra Action.

paladin/7/Oath of Devotion.note: Aura of Devotion extends charm immunity to the partner at 9m.

paladin/7/Oath of Conquest.note: Aura of Conquest deals half your paladin level in psychic to frightened creatures, so it is only as good as your Wisdom-save landing rate.

druid/1.note: Light/medium armour and shields even as a dip, plus Shillelagh, Goodberry and always-prepared Speak with Animals; Shillelagh keys off your highest spellcasting modifier, so it is not Wisdom-gated.

druid/2.note: The real dip: Wild Shape as a second HP bar that keeps your multiclass features working under the overhaul, the circle's level 2 feature, and Find Familiar always prepared.

druid/2/Circle of the Moon.note: Combat Wild Shape as a Bonus Action twice per short rest, plus Lunar Mend — the tankiest use of two levels in the class.

druid/2/Circle of the Land.note: Natural Recovery is the only in-day slot refund in the class, worth more where a long rest costs 120+ supplies.

druid/2/Circle of the Spores.note: Symbiotic Entity buys 4 temp HP per Druid level and +1d6 on weapon hits, with Halo of Spores as a reaction rider; the temp HP scales off Druid level so it is thin on a dip.

druid/2/Circle of the Stars.note: Starry Form gives Archer's bonus-action radiant, Chalice's free heal rider or Dragon's Concentration floor, plus Guidance.

druid/2/Circle of the Sea.note: Wrath of the Sea is a Wisdom-scaled bonus-action cold-and-push aura, the cheapest way to peel something off the partner.

druid/2/Circle of Stormchasers.note: Storm Shift's temp HP is 3x Druid level, so it is a rounding error on a dip and enormous as a main class.

druid/2/Circle of Winter.note: Winter Spirit adds Wisdom as cold damage to every damage spell and +1d6 on melee hits, but its 5x-Druid-level temp HP wants a main class.

druid/2/Circle of the Shepherd.note: Every Spirit Totem is an aura that buffs the other character — Bear's temp HP, Hawk's reaction advantage, Flumph's shared healing.

druid/2/Circle of Wildfire.note: A permanent extra body that casts your spells from its own position, giving a two-person party a second point of origin for AoE.

druid/2/Circle of Wrath.note: Aspects of Wrath is a self-contained scaling damage engine with no summon or gear dependency, capped by the Wisdom modifier.

druid/3.note: Feat-neutral, and adds Summon Beast and Flock of Familiars — worth it only if the build wants bodies.

druid/5.note: Conjure Animals plus Wild Strike/Extra Attack — the point where the summon economy starts carrying the duo.

druid/5/Circle of the Spores.note: Mod 4018 replaces Wild Strike with a real Extra Attack usable outside Wild Shape, which is the whole point since Symbiotic Entity does not work in beast form.

druid/6.note: The circle's tier-2 feature and the Wild Shape CR bump, both keyed to Druid level rather than character level.

druid/6/Circle of the Stars.note: Star Druid Tweaks moves Cosmic Omen onto the short rest, so it is 3-4 swings of plus-or-minus 1d6 on attacks or saves per rest cycle.

warlock/1.note: Wis + Cha saves only when first, Eldritch Blast whose beams key off character level, and one short-rest pact slot; the multiclass node grants the same light armour, so a dip frees no armour feat.

warlock/2.note: Agonizing Blast adds the Charisma modifier to every beam, making two class levels into the list's best at-will damage engine — at-will, so endurance rises with it.

warlock/1/The Hexblade.note: Hex Warrior puts Charisma on a weapon at level 1 without waiting for Pact of the Blade — the archetypal stat-gated melee dip; `cha-to-attack` marks that a second such source does nothing.

warlock/1/The Fiend.note: Dark One's Blessing is temp HP on every kill, the best defensive level 1 patron before Dark One's Own Luck arrives at 6.

warlock/1/The Archfey.note: Fey Presence is an AoE charm-or-fear on the short-rest clock — real crowd control out of a single level.

warlock/1/The Great Old One.note: Mortal Reminder fires on crits, so a multi-beam blaster triggers it far more often than the text implies.

warlock/1/The Celestial.note: Healing Light is a bonus-action heal that spends no spell slot, plus free Sacred Flame as a save-based answer to high-AC targets — but the pool is on the long-rest clock.

warlock/1/The Psyker.note: Warp detonations are free AoE, but Perils of the Warp drains your own maximum HP with no mitigation until level 10 — the file says avoid it as a dip.

warlock/3.note: Feat-neutral and the natural dip size: pact boon, 2nd-level pact slots, and Pact of the Chain's familiar as a third body on the initiative order.

warlock/5.note: Two 3rd-level slots back on every short rest, a third invocation, and Deepened Pact — Extra Attack for Blade or for the Chain familiar; it breaks the feat block unless the main class also sits on a multiple of three.

warlock/5/The Celestial.note: Revivify on a short-rest pact slot, which is the other half of the argument for a Charisma healer in a duo.

wizard/1.note: Multiclassing into Wizard grants literally nothing — no armour, no weapon, no skill, no save; the whole payload is Int spellcasting, 3 cantrips, 1 Arcane Recovery charge and the ability to transcribe Listo's abundant Wizard scrolls into a permanent library.

wizard/2.note: The school arrives at 2 and is the entire reason to stop here — the generic half is still just 1st-level slots and Savant's halved scroll-copy cost.

wizard/3.note: Feat-neutral under Listo's 3/6/9/12/13/15/18 class-level cadence, but buys only 2nd-level slots.

wizard/5.note: 3rd-level slots: Fireball, Counterspell, Haste and Animate Dead all land at once, which is the single largest jump in the class before 11.

wizard/6.note: Generic progression is flat from 5 to 6 — the level-6 school feature is the whole payload, so this breakpoint is only worth taking with a subclass part attached.

wizard/11.note: 6th-level slots plus the school capstone at 10; cantrips are on their third scaling step, so a floor of at-will damage finally exists.

wizard/14.note: Expansion's 7th-level slots at 13 and the tier-4 school feature at 14; the majority-class shape for a Wizard 14 / X 6 split.

wizard/2/Bladesinging.note: The one dip worth planning around: light armour, Performance, six martial-adjacent weapons and Bladesong (+2 AC, +2 Con saves, +3 m, advantage on Acrobatics, 2/long rest) — the cheapest AC and concentration package a full caster can buy; the invented `shield-use` tag means Bladesong is off while a shield is equipped, so it does not stack with a shield-granting part.

wizard/2/Abjuration.note: Much weaker as a dip than it looks — Arcane Ward resets to wizard level and caps at 2x wizard level, so two levels buy a 4-point shield.

wizard/6/Bladesinging.note: Bladesong to 3 uses and +3, plus Extra Attack — turns for which you would rather not burn a long-rest slot.

wizard/6/Abjuration.note: Projected Ward spends the ward, and Lone Wolf's spare Reaction, on keeping the other character alive.

wizard/6/Necromancy.note: Undead Thralls plus Animate Dead++ (free Animate Dead from 5, no cap on bodies, undead gain wizard-level HP and your proficiency to damage) — the most direct answer to two players against five-body encounters; the invented `summon-engine` tag means a second summon pool adds turn-time, not action economy.

wizard/6/Divination.note: Three Portent dice spent on Lone Wolf's second Reaction as guaranteed enemy-save failures, refunded by Expert Divination's short-rest Prophecies.

wizard/6/Transmutation.note: The Constitution-save Transmuter's Stone is the cheapest concentration insurance in the class and can be handed to the other player; the `experimental-alchemy` tag means the double-brew does not stack with the Artificer's.

wizard/6/Hierophant.note: The healer answer for a party with no cleric — Erudite Remedy heals as a bonus action and hands the target on-demand elemental resistance, plus short-rest Turn the Otherworldly.

wizard/11/Abjuration.note: Improved Abjuration recharges the ward by wizard level on every short rest, which converts Listo's 120-supply long-rest tax into a defensive resource.

wizard/11/Bladesinging.note: Bladesong at +4 AC and +4 Con saves with 4 uses, plus Song of Defence spending slots to subtract 5 damage per slot level.

wizard/11/Conjuration.note: Focused Conjuration makes damage unable to break concentration on a Conjuration spell, so the summons that are your third and fourth combatants cannot be interrupted away.

wizard/11/Necromancy.note: Inured to Undeath blanks Act 2's max-HP reduction while the uncapped undead pool scales with every slot you own.

wizard/11/Divination.note: Third Eye's simultaneous darkvision and See Invisibility on top of the Portent pool.

wizard/11/Enchantment.note: Split Enchantment doubles Hold Person and Dominate at the level encounters start fielding pairs, and Listo's Hypnotic Gaze also strips the target's concentration.

wizard/11/Evocation.note: The safe default — Sculpt Spells matters more in a duo because your partner is always inside your own fireball, and Empowered Evocation adds Int to the damage.

wizard/11/Hexcraft.note: The slot-economy school — Warlock spells and three unrestricted Eldritch Invocations, ritual-driven temp HP, and immunity to the whole charm/fear line at 10.

wizard/11/Hierophant.note: Miracleworker adds Raise Dead, Planar Binding and Dispel Evil and Good as rituals on top of a scaling bonus-action heal-plus-resistance pool.

wizard/11/School of Death.note: The highest sustained single-target damage of the schools — doubled necrotic cantrips, necrotic resistance ignored, and Arcane Recovery charges converted into damage; it gives no defensive layer at all.

wizard/14/Abjuration.note: Expansion's Spell Resistance — resistance to spell damage and advantage on every saving throw against spells and cantrips — on top of a short-rest-recharging ward.

monk/1.note: The strongest single level for any unarmoured character — 10 + DEX + WIS AC needing no proficiency and no gold at 4x prices, a bonus-action unarmed strike, and Flurry of Blows; it wants Dex and Wis both, which Lone Wolf's +4 can cover.

monk/2.note: Unarmoured Movement, Patient Defence, Step of the Wind and Listo's Uncanny Metabolism — rarely worth stopping here rather than pushing to 3.

monk/3.note: The standard dip: feat-neutral under Listo's cadence, a full subclass entry, and Deflect Missiles, all on a ki pool that refills on a short rest.

monk/5.note: Extra Attack, the d8 Martial Arts die and Stunning Strike on the WIS-driven Ki Save DC; expensive as a dip and only worth it where Monk is the main class.

monk/6.note: Ki-Empowered Strikes makes unarmed damage magical and the tier-2 subclass feature lands; the generic half adds little over 5.

monk/11.note: The d10 Martial Arts die, Evasion and Stillness of Mind from 7, and the tier-3 subclass feature — the first of the two real payoff levels.

monk/3/Way of the Friar.note: Built for exactly this run — per-turn temp HP for both characters, a free teleport to your partner, shield proficiency that still allows Unarmoured Defence plus advantage on concentration checks, and Friar's Blessing's +1d4 to attacks and saves; the invented `concentration` tag means Friar's Bond occupies the concentration slot a caster wanted.

monk/3/Way of Mercy.note: Free healing folded into Flurry plus Hands of Harm, and two skill proficiencies chosen from a list to cover gates the partner cannot roll.

monk/3/Way of the Long Death.note: Touch of Death stacks WIS + monk level temp HP on every kill; the class-defining Mastery of Death is at 11, not here.

monk/3/Way of the Astral Self.note: The single-stat Monk — the astral arms use WIS for attack and damage at +5 ft reach, so DEX and STR can both stay low and points go to CON.

monk/3/Way of the Kensei.note: Makes Monk a weapon character in a list with an enormous weapon pool and a thin unarmed one; Agile Parry's +2 AC comes free on nearly every turn.

monk/3/Way of the Open Hand.note: Topple, Push and Stagger ride every Flurry on the Ki Save DC — control that costs no extra action, which is worth more than raw damage in a two-body party.

monk/3/Way of Shadow.note: Covers the scouting role a two-person party has no body for — Hide, party-wide Pass Without Trace, Darkness and Shadow Step off one short-rest pool.

monk/3/Way of the Sun Soul.note: The only Way that makes a Monk a genuine ranged character, but Radiant Sun Bolt scales on DEX and so gains nothing from Listo's WIS-based Ki Save DC.

monk/3/Way of the Ascendant Dragon.note: Breath of the Dragon is real cone/line AoE from a class that normally has none, without spending the Bonus Action, plus a Charisma-check advantage toggle.

monk/3/Warrior of the Elements.note: Elemental Strikes replace the default unarmed attack so even opportunity attacks carry extended range and a push/pull rider, and damage type is selectable against resistant enemies.

monk/6/Way of the Friar.note: Adds quarterstaff Reach, Guiding Strike handing your partner advantage on a target, and Pacifying Sweep's arc knockback plus a Pacified rider.

monk/6/Way of Mercy.note: Physician's Touch folds condition removal — blinded, deafened, paralysed, poisoned, stunned, or all diseases — into the same free Flurry heal.

monk/6/Way of the Long Death.note: Hour of Reaping frightens everything within 30 ft on a failed WIS save, though the implementation only blocks movement toward you.

monk/6/Way of the Astral Self.note: Visage adds 120 ft darkvision through magical darkness and advantage on Insight and Intimidation, folded into the Arms bonus action.

monk/6/Way of the Kensei.note: Kensei weapons count as magical and Deft Strike spends 1 ki to add a Martial Arts die to the first hit, stacking with interrupts like Sneak Attack.

monk/11/Way of the Long Death.note: Mastery of Death is the strongest single line in the class for a two-person Lone Wolf run — 1 ki, no action, converts a drop to 0 HP into 1 HP, repeatably, from a short-rest pool.

monk/11/Way of Mercy.note: Flurry of Healing and Harm makes every Flurry strike a free full-power heal and Hands of Harm free on top, costing only short-rest ki.

monk/11/Way of the Astral Self.note: Deflect Energy reduces six damage types by 1d10 + WIS on a reaction — the best user in the class of Lone Wolf's extra Reaction — plus Empowered Arms.

monk/11/Way of the Ascendant Dragon.note: Aspect of the Wyrm is the only Way here that hands the other character a defensive buff, an elemental resistance aura, and the breath moves to three Martial Arts dice.

monk/11/Way of the Kensei.note: Sharpen the Blade spends up to 3 ki for +X attack and damage for a minute, but does nothing on a weapon that already carries an enchantment bonus.

mesmerist/1.note: Hypnotic Stare is a permanent bonus-action -1 to one enemy's saves with no resource cost, improving every control spell the duo aims at that target; whether a mid-run dip still grants the light armour, finesse weapons and skills is undocumented by the mod `(unverified)`.

mesmerist/2.note: The real dip — Towering Ego adds Cha modifier to Wisdom saves and half Cha to Intelligence saves permanently, scaling with Charisma rather than class level, so two levels buy +5 Wis at Cha 20; it shuts off while you are already under a mind-affecting condition, so it prevents rather than cures.

mesmerist/3.note: Feat-neutral under Listo's cadence and buys an Aspect, though every archetype's level-3 payload is modest and Gift of Will is out of reach until 7.

mesmerist/5.note: Hypnotic Stare goes to 2 stacks and 2nd-level Bard-list spells arrive on the half-caster table.

mesmerist/6.note: The Stare pierces mind-affecting immunity at 50% and Feint drops the target's attack rolls by 2.

mesmerist/7.note: The second real breakpoint — Tier-2 archetype picks unlock here, which is where Gift of Will and Psychic Inception live.

mesmerist/11.note: Stare to 3 stacks, Phasic Challenge, and a Tier-any archetype pick; half-caster slots mean this contributes only half to a multiclass slot table.

mesmerist/3/Aspect of the Trickster.note: Two Tier-1 Tricks implanted on yourself or the partner and six short-rest Hypnotic Bonds, firing as a free action on their trigger — Mesmeric Mirror alone is a guaranteed miss on the other character.

mesmerist/3/Aspect of the Eyebiter.note: One Tier-1 Bold Stare riding the Hypnotic Stare for its whole duration — Sundering pushes the save penalty onto AC, Disorientation onto attack and damage.

mesmerist/3/Aspect of the Daredevil.note: Two Panache and one Tier-1 Dazzling Feint; Panache only returns on a crit or kill with a one-handed piercing weapon, otherwise on a long rest, which is the expensive rest in this run.

mesmerist/5/Aspect of the Daredevil.note: Daredevil's Deeds grants Extra Attack while you hold at least 3 Panache — dedicating Panache to Improved or Greater Feints can drop you back below the threshold.

mesmerist/6/Aspect of the Eyebiter.note: Painful Stare adds 2d6 psychic once per turn whenever you damage the Stare target.

mesmerist/7/Aspect of the Trickster.note: Gift of Will adds Cha modifier plus half Mesmerist level to the partner's Wisdom save — the only partner-facing save bonus in the class, and the self-exclusion is irrelevant because Towering Ego already covers you; Compel Alacrity is a 2-round Haste on top.

mesmerist/7/Aspect of the Eyebiter.note: Psychic Inception makes the Hypnotic Stare work at full strength on normally-resistant creatures, closing the undead and construct immunity hole.

mesmerist/7/Aspect of the Daredevil.note: Parry and Riposte auto-Feints against anyone who misses you for 3 Panache, and a Tier-2 Dazzling Feint arrives.

mesmerist/11/Aspect of the Trickster.note: The strongest archetype for this run — three simultaneous implants, Expansive Trick covering both characters on one implant, and Tier-3 picks like Cursed Sanction, all off a short-rest Bond pool.

mesmerist/11/Aspect of the Eyebiter.note: The boss-lockdown option — Sapped Magic and Withering form a standing anti-caster package and Oscillation redirects a boss onto you, which needs the Resistance boon on a d8 light-armour chassis.

mesmerist/11/Aspect of the Daredevil.note: Evasion, Uncanny Dodge and a third reaction at 9 while holding 5 Panache, plus once-per-short-rest Tier-3 Feints; Superior Defense adds Charisma to AC while unarmoured.
